title: Chapter 182: Doctor Chen
html:
The black hair crashed into the old man like a wave. A slender, pale arm emerged from within it and clamped onto his shoulder, dragging him toward the dark tide. He began to tremble, clearly familiar with the hand’s strength. “I sent you out. Why did you come back?”

His answer was a brutal slam into the floor. The impact shook the corridor, and the red of his coat faded noticeably.

Zhang Ya is here!Judging by the old man’s words, he had already forced Zhang Ya out once, only for her to break through the door again.

Did you come back for me?Warmth surged through Chen Ge. He was about to speak when Zhang Ya stepped from the wave of hair. Without so much as glancing at him, she walked straight toward the old man.

A bloodcurdling scream pierced the silence behind the door, setting Chen Ge’s teeth on edge. Are all Baleful Specters this vindictive?

At full strength, the old man might have fought back. But Men Nan’s awakening had caught him off guard and reclaimed half the blood he controlled. Against Zhang Ya, he was now as helpless as a level-zero minion.

Even Red Specters must vary in strength. This old man is probably one of the weakest.

The sight of Zhang Ya eased Chen Ge’s racing heart. In this alien place, she was the only “person” who made him feel safe. Once the immediate danger had passed, he shifted the child in his arms to a more comfortable position. Looking down, he found a pair of curious, hollow sockets staring back.

Without Chen Ge noticing, the boy’s clothes had turned red. His face was deathly pale, and his eyes were entirely black—without pupils, irises, or even visible whites.

Cold sweat ran down Chen Ge’s forehead as he watched blood vessels slip back into the boy through the wound near his neck.

“I did that to wake you up; I had no choice. My intention wasn’t to harm you.”

The boy clung to him and began crawling higher. The sensation of that small body climbing over him was deeply unsettling. Chen Ge’s first instinct was to push him away, but he feared causing another misunderstanding.

“Men Nan, I know your name, and I came here to save you. A monster attacked your second personality. I’m the one who rescued him.” Chen Ge tried to earn some goodwill while he still had the chance to speak.

The old man had called the child a devil. Anyone who earned that title from a Red Specter could not be as innocent as he appeared. The boy kept climbing until his face hovered mere inches from Chen Ge’s.

At such close range, Chen Ge realized the sockets contained no eyes at all—only two hollow pits. He had no idea what the boy sought, and the hair rose along his neck. Silently, he reached into his pocket, removed the photograph of Men Nan and his mother, and slid it between their faces.

“I know about your past, and I understand your pain. If you ever need someone to talk to, you can tell me anything.” Chen Ge repeated what he had told Men Nan in the real world. “We’ve endured similar things. Perhaps we can be friends.”

Fearless truly was the best word for Chen Ge. Even now, he was considering recruiting the boy to work at the Haunted House. At the sight of his mother’s picture, the child’s demeanor softened. He released Chen Ge and dropped to the floor. “Where did you find this?”

Men Nan in the real world had asked this question before. Their way of thinking was similar.

“In the director’s dresser inside his office.”

“He dared to hide my mother’s picture.” The boy looked up. “Can I have it?”

“Of course.” Chen Ge handed it over and felt the boy’s hostility recede. Squatting to his level, he hesitated before asking softly, “The old man said this world is your nightmare, and that if you wake, the door connecting it to reality will close. Is that true?”

“This world existed before I did. I was merely the first to discover it.” The boy pocketed the photograph and fixed his hollow gaze on Chen Ge. “Don’t ask me about this place. The more you know, the harder it will be to leave.”

The child’s intelligence seemed wholly out of proportion to his appearance. From a single question, he had already discerned Chen Ge’s purpose.

“You can’t tell me anything?”

“Only that this world reflects humanity’s darkest secrets. It is filled with sin and terror. It resembles the real world but remains fundamentally different—like day and night.” The boy walked out. His red shirt was painfully bright, as though dripping with fresh blood.

“I have two more questions. Slow down.” Chen Ge hurried after him. His agility had returned, and the blood vessels that infiltrated his limbs seemed to have vanished.

The boy stopped and turned around. His empty eyes studied Chen Ge closely. “Aren’t you afraid of me?”

“I am, but I need answers.” Meeting Men Nan’s original personality carried profound significance for Chen Ge. “I want to ask about someone your second personality calls Doctor Chen.”

“Haven’t heard of him.”

“Your second personality said two people brought you back to the Third Sick Hall: the old director and this Doctor Chen.” Chen Ge spoke with complete sincerity. “He’s very important to me. He may be a missing member of my family.”

Perhaps the word family affected the boy. He turned his empty gaze aside. “Doctor Chen looked perfectly ordinary except for his eyes. He was like you—exactly the kind of person I despise.”

“That’s all?” Chen Ge fell silent before asking his second question. “How can I close the door between these two worlds for good?”

“Very simple.” The boy smiled. “Keep a living person behind the door and ask him to guard the door for you.”

“What kind of solution is that?” Chen Ge wanted to ask why the door appeared in the first place, but the boy vanished in the blink of an eye. “What is he hiding from me?”

Afraid the boy might clash with Zhang Ya, Chen Ge hurried after him.

Outside the room, he found that the child had not gone far. His brow was deeply furrowed, and his hollow gaze fixed on the scene ahead.

The red had almost vanished from the old man’s coat, and his body barely retained a human shape. Zhang Ya’s black hair engulfed what remained; he would disappear within seconds.

“Leave me the old man’s body, and I’ll let you go.” The boy was small, but Chen Ge felt the threat coming from his words.

One finger traced lips as vivid as blood. Ignoring the boy’s demand, Zhang Ya kept one foot planted on the director’s broken body and regarded the child as though she had discovered a new ingredient for dinner.
